Renal failure 2026-12-01 Medium

A machine learning-based predictive tool for complete renal response in lupus nephritis leverages the 3-month treatment milestone.

This prospective cohort study of 400 active lupus nephritis patients used machine learning to predict complete renal response at 12 months, leveraging predictors assessed at baseline and the 3-month treatment milestone. The authors developed interpretable ML models aimed at early identification of patients likely to have unfavorable renal outcomes, supporting earlier treatment decisions.

BMJ health & care informatics 2026-11-18 Medium

Comparing longitudinal regression and deep-learning models for healthcare utilisation prediction: evidence from the SHARE longitudinal panel in Europe.

This study compares classical longitudinal regression models with sequence-aware deep learning models for predicting outpatient healthcare utilisation using data from 10,777 adults in the SHARE panel across four unevenly spaced waves. It finds that deep learning does not clearly outperform simpler longitudinal models in this survey-based setting, highlighting the challenges of applying sequence models to irregularly spaced panel data. The work provides practical guidance on model choice for health-policy forecasting outside claims or EHR contexts.

Machine Learning Based Plasma Proteomic Analysis Identifies Disease Differentiating Biomarkers in Atopic Dermatitis.

This study applies machine learning to plasma proteomic data to find protein biomarkers that distinguish atopic dermatitis from ulcerative colitis, two inflammatory diseases that both involve aberrant Th2 immune activity but affect different tissues. The approach identifies disease-specific protein signatures that may help explain their distinct underlying mechanisms and improve differential diagnosis.

A Deep Learning-Based Prediction Model for Mortality in Severe COVID-19 Patients Requiring Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Multicenter Registry Analysis.

This multicenter registry study developed a deep learning model to predict mortality among critically ill COVID-19 patients admitted to the ICU, using a deliberately minimal set of readily available clinical variables to enable rapid risk stratification. The work addresses a gap in AI-based mortality prediction specifically for the ICU population, where existing evidence is limited. The emphasis on parsimonious inputs suggests the model is intended for practical bedside deployment rather than research-only use.

Cancer science 2026-11-16 Medium

MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.

MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level in silico features with patient-level mutational context, addressing the limitation of tools that ignore clinical context. This integration aims to improve variant interpretation for precision oncology, particularly for variants lacking established consensus. The approach represents a step toward context-aware computational variant assessment in cancer.

This study applies deep learning to peripheral blood smear images to predict acute inflammatory states and chronic comorbidities, moving beyond traditional morphological assessment. The authors develop and internally validate models that link immune cell morphology to systemic pathophysiology, suggesting PBS images contain predictive information beyond standard clinical use.

Cell 2026-11-12 High

Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia.

This study built a single-cell multi-omic atlas combining histone modification profiles and transcriptomes across eight human basal ganglia regions from neurotypical donors. It maps cell-type- and region-specific active and repressive regulatory elements and gene regulatory networks, revealing combinatorial homeobox transcription factor expression underlying cell identity. The resource provides a foundation for understanding basal ganglia function and dysfunction in neurological and psychiatric disorders.

Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.

This study integrates single-cell and bulk multi-omics data to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, identifying C16orf74 as a previously uncharacterized regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The authors show that C16orf74 expression is associated with EMT-associated malignant states and has prognostic relevance, suggesting it could serve as a clinically accessible biomarker in HNSCC.

Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) 2026-11-10 Medium

EZpred: Improving Deep Learning-Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs.

EZpred is a deep learning method that improves enzyme function prediction (EC number assignment) by incorporating features from unlabeled sequence homologs, analogous to how AlphaFold uses homologous sequences for structure prediction. Unlike prior models that rely only on labeled homologs, EZpred leverages unlabeled homologs to boost accuracy. This demonstrates that homology-aware features can significantly enhance functional annotation.

Molecular biomedicine 2026-11-09 Medium

Preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian masses using cfDNA fragmentomics and serum biomarkers.

This multicenter study developed a diagnostic model combining cfDNA fragmentomic features (fragment size, nucleosome footprints, copy-number variations, repeat element patterns) from low-pass whole-genome sequencing with serum biomarkers to distinguish malignant from benign ovarian masses. The stacked machine learning model was trained and validated across 743 participants in multiple cohorts, addressing the clinical challenge of ambiguous preoperative diagnosis when standard serum markers are uninformative.

Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics and Prenatal Medicine: Current Evidence, Clinical Validation and Implementation.

This review surveys the current evidence for AI applications in obstetrics and prenatal medicine, covering prenatal ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, fetal MRI, genomic screening, risk prediction, and clinical decision support. It emphasizes the state of clinical validation and the practical requirements for implementing these tools in routine prenatal care.

Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data.

The authors present a method that combines graph theory and machine learning to estimate the growth rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineages from genetic sequence data. By representing distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians, they extract features that identify lineages undergoing rapid population growth, enabling real-time monitoring of emerging variants from large genomic data streams.

Integrated multi-omics identifies PTGDS-enriched mature oligodendrocyte state remodeling in paraquat-associated Parkinson's disease.

Persistent atrial fibrillation in older adults: Comparison of seven models and development of a gradient boosting machine classifier in a single-center observational study.

This single-center observational study of 572 older adults compared seven classification models for identifying persistent atrial fibrillation and developed an interpretable gradient boosting machine classifier. The work identifies clinical correlates of persistent AF and demonstrates that a GBM approach can classify patients, though the single-center design and modest sample size limit generalizability.

Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.

This scoping review maps the literature (2021–2026) on computational methods for discovering plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening 5062 records down to 79 charted sources. It characterizes the composition of the field—mostly primary studies, with smaller shares of tool/database papers—and assesses reporting practices. The work provides a structured overview of an emerging area rather than new experimental findings.

SeqBattNet: A discrete-state physics-informed neural network with aging adaptation for battery modeling.

The paper introduces SeqBattNet, a physics-informed neural network that models battery behavior using discrete states and incorporates adaptation to battery aging. It aims to overcome limitations of existing model-based and data-driven approaches, such as heavy parameter requirements and dependence on large labeled datasets, for tasks like predicting remaining discharge time and energy.
